summary: I reject revision 2 because of one major finding. Every finding from review 2 is resolved, though the run log from review 2's minor finding is still not cited. The denylist is gone. gateWorkflowProblems now checks every workflow, job and step key against allowlists, and it checks each action's inputs too (workflow-check.mjs:350-399). The Gates test now pins the step sequence, including action names (workflow-check.test.mjs:99-101). I traced review 2's reproduction, `defaults.run.shell: 'true {0}'`. It now reports 'The Gates workflow sets defaults:'. The same holds for env at every level, working-directory, container, an extra action, a checkout ref, any other run command, an upload without if:, and step `id`, `shell` or `timeout-minutes`. I found no YAML form, expression, trigger or key that gets past the checker. Revision checks 12-16 hold. The evidence binds to 98fa147. The binding log records HEAD 98fa147 and an empty status for every source root, including ignored files, one second before the receipts. The checker and test blobs at 98fa147 (48c7cbf, dc421bf, read from the GitHub API) match the worker's tests-after log. No later commit touches tools/workflow-check.mjs. The blocking problem is action identity. gateWorkflowProblems and the sequence test look only at the part of `uses:` before '@'. workflowProblems requires only some 40-hex SHA. GitHub fetches an action at any commit in the repository's fork network (the 'impostor commit' behavior that Chainguard published in 2023). So replacing the setup-node or checkout SHA with a commit pushed to a fork, under a plausible '# v7.x' comment, makes both checkers report nothing and keeps every controller test passing. That action can then write a `node` shim to GITHUB_PATH, or write NODE_OPTIONS or BASH_ENV to GITHUB_ENV. Every later gate step would then exit 0 without running its gate. This contradicts the claim at workflow-check.mjs:347 and tools/README.md:173 that no 'other action can change what a gate step runs'. A minor gap remains for check 5. There is no `gh run view` record for the revision 2 integration. When I checked, Gates run 37884244035 for 586b854 had the Linux job succeeded and the Windows job still running. I ran no shell commands. My conclusions about checker behavior come from tracing the code, not from executing it.

criteria.criterion: Review 2 major: the Gates workflow is checked against key allowlists, not a denylist
criteria.evidence: Allowlists cover workflow keys (workflow-check.mjs:354), job keys (:361), action-step keys and inputs (:369-382), run-step keys (:390) and the run command (:393). An upload step must set if: ${{ always() }} (:384-386). By tracing: defaults, env, working-directory, container, strategy, services, needs, outputs, id, shell, timeout-minutes and continue-on-error at any level each produce a problem.

criteria.criterion: No Gates step can exit 0 without running its gate while gateWorkflowProblems and workflowProblems report nothing

See the major finding. I found no other route through keys, inputs, expressions, environment-file writes or YAML forms.

findings.issue: Action identity is bound only by owner/repo, never by commit. gateWorkflowProblems computes `uses.value.value.split('@')[0]` (line 370). The Gates sequence test also compares only `field(s,'uses')?.split('@')[0]` (workflow-check.test.mjs:99). workflowProblems requires only some 40-hex SHA and some version comment (lines 317-318). GitHub fetches `owner/repo@<sha>` for any commit in the repository's fork network (Chainguard, 'What the fork? Imposter commits in GitHub Actions and CI/CD', 2023). Reproduction, traced and not executed: push to a fork of actions/setup-node a commit whose action writes `$RUNNER_TEMP/shim` to GITHUB_PATH, where shim/node(.cmd) exits 0. Alternatively, it writes `NODE_OPTIONS=--require=…` or `BASH_ENV=…` to GITHUB_ENV. In gates.yml, replace `actions/setup-node@949feb24…` with `actions/setup-node@<fork-sha> # v7.1.1`. Both checkers then report nothing: the SHA is 40-hex, the comment matches VERSION_COMMENT, the action is accepted, and the input is node-version. Case 1 and the Gates sequence test still pass. On GitHub, every later `node tools/fairpane.mjs run <gate>` step resolves `node` to the shim and exits 0 without running its gate. The same applies to the checkout SHA. This contradicts the doc comment at workflow-check.mjs:347 and tools/README.md:173 ('No … other action can therefore change what a gate step runs'). It also contradicts contract revision 2's 'The only accepted actions are actions/checkout …, actions/setup-node …, actions/upload-artifact'. Review 2 recommended matching the full sequence 'uses and all'. The revision matches only the action names.
findings.recommendation: Bind each accepted Gates action to its reviewed commit. For example, make GATE_ACTIONS map the full `owner/repo@sha` (or name to an allowed SHA list) and report any other ref. Alternatively, have the Gates test assert the exact `uses` strings, as REVIEWED does for problem lists. Then add a step to the pin-update procedure (tools/README.md:179-185) that edits the reviewed SHA together with the workflow, and add a fixture that changes only the SHA and must report a problem. Otherwise, narrow workflow-check.mjs:347, tools/README.md:173 and the contract wording to say that the code an accepted action runs depends on the pinned SHA being reviewed by hand against the release tag.

findings.issue: Each case stops at its first failing assertion. So the baseline shows case 12 red only for the workflow-level defaults fixture. It does not show the remaining 14 fixtures (job defaults, env, working-directory, container, checkout ref, commands, upload without if) failing against the old checker. By tracing ef953b17's gateStepProblems, most of them would also have reported nothing, so the red baseline is valid but coarse.
findings.recommendation: For future baselines of multi-fixture cases, record a per-fixture result, or split such cases so each fixture's red state is observable.
